key_insight: First-principles spin-orbit calculations show that chiral hybrid perovskites ($R$/$S$-PEA)PbI$_3$ and ($R$/$S$-NEA)PbI$_3$ both host strong spin-split bands, but the magnitude and spin textures depend on molecular choice and chirality-driven octahedral distortions.
engineering_relevance: Understanding how ligand chirality and band hybridization tune spin splitting can guide the design of perovskite optoelectronic devices with controllable spin and circular-dichroic responses.
method: DFT calculations including spin-orbit coupling on one-dimensional chiral perovskites
Compare band structures, spin splitting, and spin textures for PEA- vs NEA-based compounds
Use group-theoretical analysis of space group $P2_12_12_1$ to explain degeneracies and band sticking
evidence_signal: The abstract reports stronger valence-edge spin splitting in ($R$/$S$-NEA)PbI$_3$ than in ($R$/$S$-PEA)PbI$_3$, with opposite spin textures for opposite molecular handedness and symmetry-enforced features at Brillouin-zone boundaries.
watch_item: The results are theoretical and material-specific, so device-level performance and experimental stability still need validation.
paper_title: First-principles calculations of spin-split bands in chiral hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites ($R$/$S$-PEA)PbI$_3$ and ($R$/$S$-NEA)PbI$_3$
